correctness.rationale: For \(m\) with \(\omega(m)\le2\), parity excludes even \(m\), the unit \(m=1\) is checked, and \(\sigma(p^e)/p^e<p/(p-1)\le3/2\) excludes every odd prime power. For the two primes \(5\le p<q\), the multiplicative ratio is strictly less than \(35/24<3/2\). Hence \(m=3^a q^b\); exact algebra reduces its equation to \((3^{a+1}-q)(q^b-1)=4(q-1)\). The first factor is a positive integer, so \(b\ge2\) would require it to equal \(4/(1+q+\cdots+q^{b-1})<1\), impossible. Thus \(b=1\) and \(q=3^{a+1}-4\) prime; direct substitution proves the reverse implication. The standalone verifier enumerated 367461 integers with \(\omega\le2\) through \(10^6\), finding exactly \(15,207,19359\) in both sets, and certifies the larger witness by exhaustive trial division. There is no finite-to-infinite inference.

originality.rationale: The known OEIS/Guy–Shanks family is credited as a sufficient construction, not claimed as new. The theorem adds an unrestricted necessity statement in the entire \(\omega\le2\) layer. Checked primary works supply finite tables or impose an additional neighbor-primality condition; the closest published result bounds \(\Omega\) on both adjacent integers and cannot cover repeated-power examples. Searches included equivalent normalizations, stronger classifications and exact database statements. Unindexed duplication is a residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed earlier classification of this elementary omega<=2 slice might exist.
The theorem makes no claim of infinitely many primes 3^(a+1)-4 or of completeness for omega>=3.

value.rationale: The recorded generalized perfect-number equation has numerous examples of differing prime support and a prominent known prime construction. Proving this construction exhaustive for all positive m with at most two distinct prime factors resolves an infinite natural structural stratum, eliminates all competing prime-power and two-support shapes, and removes the unrelated neighbor-primality restriction. The exact distinct-support invariant is motivated by the known families and by the incompleteness of finite tables, not an arbitrary numerical cutoff. The unresolved three-or-more-support problem is explicitly excluded.
